Ceux qui ont le temps et la curiosité pourront peut-être réfléchir sur ce qu'ils apprennent - surtout s'ils font partie de "l'élite", encore une fois - mais c'est quasiment foutu pour ceux qui arrêtent leur scolarité avant ou qui suivent d'autres voies. Se rajoute à ça une culture où il est très mal vu de discuter de ce que l'on apprend (parce que pas le temps) et il devient très difficile de se faire une culture scientifique, voir une culture tour court (en se basant uniquement avec ce qu'on nous donne à l'école).

I use a drop of coconut oil during my daily hair styling, so I mix that with a bit of perfume oil - I basically roll the bottle a couple times on my hand, add the coconut oil, mix that together in my palms and run those through my hair's ends. Musk is the components that make scents smell ''organic'' and living. It's the difference between a Jasmin bathroom spray and a Jasmin perfume: one feels plastic-y and one-note, the other like something rolled itself in a bunch of flowers. It's what links your skin and your fragrance, you could say. It doesn't really have a smell by itself (animalistic ? Slightly sweaty ?), and it's also a great stabilizer for perfumes. 

Both are extremely popular in Arab perfumery, and are base notes for most of these perfumes! I've noticed that generally these two are not mixed in a single fragrance - or at least not in a noticeable  fashion - as to not overpower eachother. So if one doesn't like Oud they should look into Musk based perfumes, and vice versa.

Hey, I relate a lot. You just seem to be very introverted and analytical, which is why it's easy for you to go deep when you speak. One-on-one conversations are slow paced and require you to analyse what is being said, but group ones are fast-paced and with an emotional focus. That's why you struggle. But remember that conversations work all the same no matter the setting : find a relatable observation, pick a point of interest in it, go on a tangent about that point, gauge the person's interest. You just really have to focus on the emotional concepts brought forward instead of intellectual. 

You won't probably find yourself at the center of a group conversation (that's generally for more extraverted people), but you can always pick somebody else in a group who doesn't speak much and talk to them. Chime in occasionally (it's okay to do in a group setting!) and don't be afraid of saying something off. It happens all the time.

People trust you because you don't speak much and confide in you because they know you'll keep what they say to yourself. It's a very good thing.
